blockers.what_was_tried: (i) An inventory of the deletion layer: LadderPump.lean carries single-step deletion admissibility (exists_deleted_ladderPath_of_pend_past) and the deletion type lemma (tpOf_eq_delIdx_of_tpOf_eq), but NO iterated deletion (no mirror of exists_iterSpliced_ladderPath_of_pend_past) and no downward assembly; the single-step lemma also fixes the deleted path's register base at nxtAt g (l : ℤ) rather than prescribing the register at the compared position. (ii) The register-rebuild step was then attempted directly, feeding the deleted walk to exists_ladderPath_of_walk_nxt with n₀ := nxtAt g 0, which compiles down to exactly the one goal quoted above.
blockers.why_it_failed: For a ≤ v the deleted walk's pin v IS the original's pin v + l, and delCnt g a l (v + 1) = cntAt g (v + l + 1), so the bound DEMANDED is |cntAt g (v + l + 1) − nxtAt g 0| ≤ |v| while the original path supplies only |cntAt g (v + l + 1) − nxtAt g 0| ≤ |v + l| (pinCompat_of_ladderPath, nxtAt_lipschitz_two_sided). The demand exceeds the supply by exactly l, and by exactly m*(P+1) when iterated m*(P+1)/l times. That gap is the FORWARD register cascade, the second side of this task's two-sided open core, and it is not slack a sharper proof recovers: the tight doubling chain has Lipschitz slack exactly 0 at every gap between pins (tightChain_slack_zero), so the demanded bound fails there for every m ≥ 1. The pin-free hypothesis the phase was to carry constrains the PAST; the obstruction lives among the pins ABOVE, and forward pin-freeness is a property of a PATH, not of a counter state, while cellAt quantifies over EVERY path through the state.
